answer: Each newcomer signs a sonnet naming the ocean that staked it. That ocean locks nectar for every sonnet it backs: n identities in one epoch lock base×2^(n−1), forfeited whole if any one is proven fake. Forking fresh oceans fails — each child draws its nectar from a parent whose depth must cover all descendants — so a k-th clone forces the root ocean's lock from base×2^(k−1) to base×2^k every epoch. A newcomer on an empty lineage locks base.
